topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms and deterministic operation-path joining
questions: Are user information, query, fragment, percent-encoded path separators and non-root base paths allowed in api_base_url, and precisely how are trailing slashes removed and the path joined?

Are userinfo, a base path, query, fragment, repeated trailing slashes, Unicode hosts and noncanonical IP forms allowed, and exactly how are joining, Host construction and loopback classification performed for them?

Are user information, query, fragment, an existing base path, percent escapes, IPv6 zone identifiers, or multiple trailing slashes allowed, and exactly how is the base URL joined to the operation path?

judgement.why: This asks the same base-URL grammar and joining question already judged in P4, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Valid service base URLs and deterministic joining with operation paths
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Canonical multipart serialization, escaping, filenames, and boundary selection
questions: What happens when a port name contains a quote, backslash, control character, non-ASCII text or another character requiring Content-Disposition escaping?
How are multipart names and filenames escaped, how is the boundary chosen, and what happens when a name or content cannot be serialized unambiguously?
What exact multipart serialization must every implementation produce, and how is a boundary selected so it cannot occur ambiguously in part content?

judgement.why: This asks the same multipart escaping, boundary and serialization question already judged in P5, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Validation, escaping, and wire serialization of multipart requests
precedent.why: Multipart wire serialization, escaping, boundary generation and request-description encoding are State 6 format and encoding matters.

topics.topic: Detection and classification of sandbox resource-limit hits
questions: What observable evidence constitutes a limit hit when the OS reports an allocation or fork failure, the program catches that failure, the process is killed, or a timeout and limit event occur at nearly the same time?
How does the parent determine that a memory, process or scratch limit was hit when the sandboxed code catches the resulting error?
What exactly counts as a limit being hit, and how does the parent reliably distinguish a caught limit denial from an ordinary exception or successful execution?

judgement.why: This asks the same resource-limit detection and precedence question already judged in P26, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Detection and precedence of resource-limit hits caught by user code
quotes:
Outcomes are closed and checked in this order, the first that holds
   deciding: wall deadline passed — `timeout`; a limit hit (memory, process count,
   scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; a trap of rule 4 raised —
   `sandbox_violation`; the module failed to load, has no `run`, raised, or the
   process exited abnormally — `crashed`;
precedent.why: Reliable detection distinguishing a limit hit from a crash was already required by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Filesystem access permitted to sandboxed function code
questions: May agent code read or write arbitrary paths inside the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files, or only use the input and output objects supplied by the runner?
May function code create, enumerate and read arbitrary files in the exchange directory or runtime, or may it access only the specific input and output artifacts supplied by the runner?
May agent code open and inspect files in the runtime or exchange directory, or must all filesystem access by agent code be refused?

judgement.why: This asks the same sandbox filesystem-access question already judged in P3, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Permitted filesystem access for sandboxed function code
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Guaranteeing deterministic execution of allowed Python code
questions: How is determinism guaranteed or refused for arbitrary standard-library Python that can use thread scheduling, process scheduling, object identities and other nondeterministic observations not trapped by A03?
What prevents allowed Python code from producing different outcomes for the same implementation and inputs?

What rule prevents code from using values such as process identifiers, object identities, filesystem metadata or ordering, locale, interpreter/platform facts, or other standard-library state to produce different outputs for equal inputs?

judgement.why: This asks the same deterministic-execution enforcement question already judged in P1, and the relevant requirement has not changed.

precedent.topic: Enforcement and failure handling for deterministic function execution
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Reading and validating manifests at the configured revision
questions: How is a file read “at” manifest_revision without changing the working tree, and what is refused when the location is not a repository or the revision cannot be resolved?
How does the kernel resolve and verify `manifest_revision` when reading a manifest record, rather than merely reading the current file at `manifest_location`?
What mechanism selects the configured revision, and how are a missing revision, non-repository location, checkout failure, or revision/path mismatch classified?

judgement.why: This asks the same configured-manifest-revision question already judged in P10, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Loading, validation, and change semantics of the configured manifest revision
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
precedent.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

judgement.failure: a passage the precedent quotes is no longer found verbatim

topics.topic: Tie-breaking order for edges and constants in flow identity and proof
questions: How are identity lists ordered when those sort keys tie, such as legal edges with the same endpoints but different guard values or duplicate constants aimed at one port?
How are edges or constants whose stated sort keys are equal ordered for hashing and for selecting the first proof failure?
How are edges or constants ordered when those keys are equal, particularly allowed parallel guarded edges with different guard values and multiple constants targeting the same port?

judgement.why: This asks the same tied-edge and tied-constant ordering question already judged in P6, and the relevant identity-ordering passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Canonical ordering of tied edges and constants for identity and proof checks
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Accepted manifest structure and classification order for malformed records
questions: What complete manifest shape is accepted, and does malformed data in an unrelated capability or instance invalidate the record or only the selected operation and instance?
Which structural and type errors make the record a manifest mismatch, in what order are they checked, and which detail is reported first?

judgement.why: This asks the same manifest-shape and malformed-record ordering question already judged in P15, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Valid manifest record shapes and classification order for malformed records
precedent.why: The exact manifest schema, nested field types and malformed-shape validation belong to State 6.

topics.topic: Definition and DNS handling of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: What counts as a loopback host: only literal IPv4 and IPv6 loopback addresses, or also names that resolve to loopback, and when is resolution checked?
Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, the hostname `localhost`, or any hostname whose DNS resolution currently yields a loopback address, and how are mixed or changing DNS answers handled?

judgement.why: This asks the same loopback-host and DNS-handling question already judged in P9, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Host forms and DNS behavior qualifying for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Deterministic startup recovery ordering and advancement before opening the surface
questions: What is the deterministic order of all startup checks, temporary/spool cleanup, in-flight conversion and run advancement, and which failure is reported when several fail?
After restart, should a run that has a waiting element and an independent ready element advance the ready element before the surface opens?

quotes:
The order of process start, every step required, as "Start" above lists it: installation,
the installed instances, store, sandbox probe, `in_flight` recovery, run
recovery, and only then the first request (A03 rule 8, A09 rule 1, A14 rule 5,
A18).

`capability:runs.recover_running_runs`: first names to
   `capability:store.remove_run_spool` every ended run that does not keep its
   spool (A14 rule 4, A18 rule 4); then derives every run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval`
   or `pending` — from its records, oldest first, rewriting a lagging status
   or waiting point and reaching again, through
   `capability:effects.reach_operation_element`, an operation element whose
   wait no longer holds (A14 rule 5); then, as the kernel actor, advances every
   run left `running`, oldest first: a function element without a concluded
   record is executed again; a `read` element without one is sent again; an
   operation element of another class with neither a concluded record nor an
   EffectAttempt is reached as for the first time, an unused approval covering
   it only while the rebuilt request has its `request_digest` (A14 rule 5).
judgement.why: The later module and flow texts fix the complete startup sequence and say that recovery advances only runs whose re-derivation leaves them running.

topics.topic: Exact sampling events and transaction sharing for timestamps
questions: At which exact event is each requested_at, started_at, ended_at, recorded_at, concluded_at, activated_at and similar timestamp sampled, and do fields written in one transaction share one reading or use separate readings?
Does `concluded_at` remain the time the transport outcome became unknown, change to the owner's resolution time, or is a separate resolution timestamp required?

quotes:
Every timestamp an operation records comes from
  `clock.kernel_now`, taken at the moment the field names: a `started_at` when
  the execution or send begins — for an operation's NodeExecution, the
  `recorded_at` of its EffectAttempt when it has one (A11 rule 4) — every other
  time when its store change is made.

resolve_unknown_outcome: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write exactly one ResolveAttemptChange carrying the attempt key and the resolution, applied or not_applied, and return the EffectAttempt as written with resolved_by set; it writes no NodeExecution, so the attempt's one NodeExecution keeps outcome_unknown and the resolution is recorded nowhere else.

record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.
judgement.why: The later API fixes timestamp sampling, and resolution changes only the resolution fields, leaving the attempt's existing concluded_at unchanged.

topics.topic: Ownership, permissions, ACLs, and recursion required for private data storage
questions: Which owners, permission bits, ACLs and directory traversal permissions satisfy “private,” and is the check recursive over all existing entries?
What exact ownership and permission checks apply to the directory, database, value area, fixtures, spool directories, lock file, and their ancestors?

judgement.why: This asks the same filesystem ownership and privacy-check question already judged in P12, and the relevant passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Ownership, permissions, links, and file types required for data-directory privacy
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Recovering the exact FlowActivation authorizing a draft-write attempt
questions: How is the exact FlowActivation used as a draft-write attempt’s authority recovered after the same version has been deactivated and activated again?
How can a later draft-write send recover the exact FlowActivation when the same flow version may have been deactivated and activated again after the run started?

judgement.why: This asks the same durable FlowActivation-identification question already judged in P19, and the relevant later-state decision has not changed.

precedent.topic: Durable identification of the exact FlowActivation authorizing draft-write sends
quotes:
Which FlowActivation a `draft-write` send names** (A10 rule 6): the latest
   FlowActivation of the run's pinned version before the Run record in store
   order — the one under which it started. `runs` finds it and passes it to
   `effects` with every call about one of the run's elements (State 3, "Facts
   passed down"); store order, not time, so two records never tie.
precedent.why: The later API text identifies the authorizing activation by its store position immediately before the Run record.

topics.topic: Retention and replacement semantics for unnamed failed-attempt spool files
questions: What is a spool “position” for an unnamed failed-attempt file, and can a later attempt with a different attempt_number ever write that same position?
After a non-spool-ceiling failure, are files produced by that failed attempt deleted immediately or retained unnamed until the run spool is removed or the position is replaced?

quotes:
An element that does not
      succeed keeps no output: its NodeExecution names none, a value it produced
   is not stored, and the files its attempt spooled are discarded with no
   SpooledFile record naming them.

A spool-ceiling refusal removes that
   attempt's files at once (A15 rule 3); after any other failure they stay in
   the run's spool unnamed, counted toward `spool_run_bytes_max`, until that
   spool is removed (A18 rule 4) or a later write to the same position
   replaces them.
judgement.why: One passage says a failed element's spooled files are discarded, while the other says they remain unnamed after every failure except a spool-ceiling refusal.

topics.topic: Whether seeded pseudorandom APIs are permitted
questions: Does “no randomness” prohibit every pseudo-random API, or only nondeterministic entropy sources?
Is deterministic pseudorandom generation part of the permitted function language, or is every randomness API forbidden regardless of seeding?

quotes:
`random.Random(seed)`
   with an explicit seed stays usable: it draws no entropy, so equal inputs
   still give equal outputs, which is what State 0's "no randomness" asks.
judgement.why: The text explicitly permits explicitly seeded deterministic pseudorandom generation and explains that the prohibition concerns entropy-based nondeterminism.

topics.topic: Application of lowered release ceilings to persisted artifacts
questions: After an upgrade lowers a non-contract ceiling, may existing oversized records still be inspected, admitted, activated, or run, and at which operation is a new limit applied?

topics.topic: Atomic validation and delivery behavior for mapped output aggregates
questions: Are all mapped output lists validated before any is delivered, and can valid sibling outputs or flow outputs remain produced when another aggregate is oversized?

topics.topic: Continuation and scan semantics for filtered pagination
questions: What continuation token is returned when a filtered page finds no matching item before reaching the scan limit but older records may still match, and does page_size limit matched items or records scanned?

topics.topic: Disclosure classification of an empty mapped-operation output list
questions: What disclosure class does an empty output list of a mapped operation node receive?

topics.topic: Encoding and validity rules for HTTP header values
questions: What character encoding and validity rules apply to required-header and credential values, and what outcome applies when an accepted value cannot be represented verbatim by the HTTP transport?

topics.topic: Exact audit events and operations treated as sandbox violations
questions: Which exact CPython audit events and operations count as socket, subprocess, ctypes and file-opening violations, including os.fork, Unix sockets, dynamic loading and descriptor-based file access?

topics.topic: Exact canonical JSON used for an EffectAttempt idempotency key
questions: What exact JSON value is canonicalized to produce the idempotency key, including the field names and manifest field order?

topics.topic: Exact pinned CPython and bubblewrap release versions
questions: Which exact CPython patch version and bubblewrap version are part of release v1, and must startup refuse other versions?

topics.topic: Exposure and verification of mapped aggregate failure reasons
questions: How is the mapped node's derived failure and reason exposed and verified, especially for an agent that cannot receive personal-data values or identifiers needed to recompute the list?

topics.topic: Handling malformed or unsupported FlowConstant schemas
questions: What happens when a constant's declared schema is malformed or outside the supported schema subset, given that the kernel must validate the value against it before keeping the version?

topics.topic: Handling unsupported flow input or output schemas
questions: May a flow version declare an unsupported schema, and if not, is that refused before the version is kept or returned as a proof failure?

topics.topic: Manifest instances included in the startup credential-header collision check
questions: At startup, which manifest instance records are read for this collision check, and what happens if one is absent, malformed or cannot be read?

topics.topic: Meaning and validation of a file port's value_schema
questions: What does value_schema constrain on a file port, and what does it mean for a file fixture or file value to fit that schema?

topics.topic: NodeExecution value/entity semantics and identity
questions: Is a NodeExecution a value record or an entity/observation, and what is its identity?

topics.topic: Ordering derived terminal records relative to ready-node execution
questions: When some nodes are ready to execute while other nodes have just become skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed, are all derived terminal records written before selecting the next ready node, after it, or interleaved by node_id?

topics.topic: Outcome when an HTTP response body fails after final status and headers
questions: If a final 4xx, 3xx, 5xx or 2xx status and headers arrive but the body stalls, resets or times out, does the status row decide the outcome or is there no valid final response?

topics.topic: Outcome when trial output exceeds storage but not contract limits
questions: What outcome and detail apply when a trial returns a schema-valid value below its contract output bound but above `stored_value_bytes_max`?

topics.topic: Required completeness and exclusivity of TrialCase inputs and expected outputs
questions: Must trial inputs contain exactly every input port and no extras, and, when expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly every output port?

topics.topic: Required installation-token encoding and entropy
questions: Must tokens be valid unpadded base64url decoding to at least 32 bytes, or is a length of 43 arbitrary characters sufficient?

topics.topic: Retry semantics after a service_unreachable NodeExecution
questions: Does a `service_unreachable` NodeExecution conclude the element permanently, or is it a concluded attempt while the element itself remains retryable?

topics.topic: Scratch accounting and pre-execution staging-limit outcomes
questions: What occupies the scratch budget, and what outcome is recorded when preparing the sandbox exceeds it before user code starts?

topics.topic: Start, end, and scope of the HTTP transport deadline
questions: From what event to what event is transport_timeout_ms measured, and is it one total deadline or separate DNS, connect, write, header and body deadlines?

topics.topic: Storage and delivery of TrialExecution exception diagnostics
questions: Where is a trial execution’s bounded exception diagnostic recorded and returned to the repairing agent?

topics.topic: Unit used to measure and truncate redacted failure details
questions: Is failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values or characters after replacement and truncation?

topics.topic: Validity and ordering of empty node identifiers
questions: Is an empty node_id allowed, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against a flow endpoint?

topics.topic: Whether all clock and timing sources must be blocked
questions: Does the closed trap list take precedence even though CPython 3.12 exposes other timing sources such as thread_time, clock_gettime, os.times and resource usage, or must every usable clock source be blocked?

topics.topic: Whether file outputs may serve as guards and when they are refused
questions: Can a file output be used as a guard, and if not, at which proof check is it refused?

topics.topic: Whether invalid Python is rejected during authoring or later validation
questions: Is syntactically invalid or unloadable Python refused by the authoring action, or stored and rejected only by trial/admission?

topics.topic: Whether multipart framing changes invalidate approval
questions: Does a changed multipart boundary or resulting Content-Length invalidate an approval?
